description: The public Zenodo DamCrack release contains drone and smartphone images of cracks and spalling on a concrete dam in Spokane, Washington. Its article describes overlapping aerial images for possible three-dimensional photogrammetry and 11,288 curated images for classification, detection and segmentation. Zenodo lists four ZIP archives, including a separate 3D model package, under CC BY 4.0. These are visual and geometric survey inputs for dam damage assessment, not measured leakage, structural strength or failure probabilities. One dam, lighting variation, image annotation and camera geometry are limitations for transferring damage scores to a fleet. A reviewer-assessed use is testing 2D defect recognition or 3D surface reconstruction before assigning a dam-condition state in a simulation. data-bc-mines-dam-safety-inspection-reports-summary is a related inspection resource without image-level linkage. The article compares DamCrack with the separate DamSegment dataset and reports different sizes and capture methods, so the two releases are kept distinct. No image or 3D archive was downloaded. Geographic coverage is the single surveyed Spokane dam.
